headline: Loon Mountain proposes fourth peak in expansion that could reshape Lincoln ski traffic
dek: The Lincoln resort says the plan would add 280 acres, four lifts and two lodges, but the project still faces a federal environmental review and has no construction timetable.
body: Loon Mountain Resort has submitted a proposal to add a fourth lift-served peak overlooking downtown Lincoln, a long-range plan that would substantially enlarge one of New Hampshire’s most visible ski destinations if it clears federal and local reviews. The resort says the concept would add 280 acres of skiable terrain and bring its potential total to 955 acres, a 137% increase over the terrain now available.

The proposal was announced Oct. 6 by [Loon Mountain Resort](https://www.loonmtn.com/latest-news/pr-peak-4) and independently reported by [WCVB](https://www.wcvb.com/article/loon-mountain-fourth-peak-expansion/74057822). The new terrain would sit west of the resort’s current South Peak footprint, with views toward Lincoln’s town center. The announcement is important for the region because it describes a possible new visitor draw and a direct relationship between a major mountain expansion, downtown access and the future shape of tourism in the Pemigewasset Valley.

Loon’s concept calls for 145 acres of traditional trails and another 135 acres of tree-skiing areas. Four aerial lifts would serve roughly 1,500 vertical feet, and the resort proposes a summit lodge at an elevation of about 2,324 feet with dining, sightseeing and event space. A second lodge is envisioned at mid-mountain. The resort says the layout is meant to give skiers and snowboarders more room to progress beyond beginner terrain while also adding winding trails, open cruisers and more challenging woods skiing.

That design would make the project more than a simple trail cut. It would create a separate operating area with new lifts, buildings and connections to the existing resort network. The ski-industry publication [PeakRankings](https://www.peakrankings.com/content/loon-proposes-massive-fourth-peak-expansion) described the proposal as an unusually large Eastern resort expansion, while also emphasizing that the drawings are conceptual and could change. Loon has not announced a project cost, a first construction phase or an opening season.

The immediate next step is a federal Environmental Assessment because most of the proposed terrain lies within the White Mountain National Forest. Loon says the U.S. Forest Service has accepted the proposal for review and that the assessment is expected to take about 12 months. The review will be followed by additional federal and local permitting decisions; acceptance for review is not approval to build. The process is where questions about forest impacts, water, wildlife, visual changes, transportation and public access can be examined before any construction schedule is set.

Land ownership adds another layer. Loon says the project area includes both national-forest land and private property owned by South Peak Resort, an independently operated business. Neither Loon nor South Peak owns all of the land involved, so the proposal depends on coordination among the resort, the private landowner, the Forest Service and local authorities. The resort says any buildout would be phased and adjusted in response to public feedback, operating needs and environmental findings.

For Lincoln, the potential payoff is a larger year-round tourism asset, but the impacts would not be limited to the slopes. A new peak facing downtown could send more visitors through local businesses and create demand for lodging, food and services. It could also intensify longstanding practical questions about parking, road congestion, employee housing and the balance between resort growth and the town’s capacity. Those effects remain projections, not measured outcomes, because the resort has not submitted a final construction plan or visitor forecast.

The announcement also sits within Loon’s broader Flight Path: 2030 investment plan. The resort separately says a 272-acre Black Ridge tree-skiing expansion is planned for the 2027-28 winter season, along with projects involving lifts, summer activities and snowmaking. Peak 4 is distinct from that work and is much less certain. Loon says the fourth-peak concept grew from 1960s drawings associated with founder and former New Hampshire Gov. Sherman Adams, but the historical vision does not reduce the modern project’s permitting requirements.

For now, skiers have a proposal, not a new mountain. The environmental assessment, public process and local approvals will determine whether the concept changes, moves forward in phases or stops. The next meaningful milestones will be the Forest Service’s review materials and opportunities for public comment, followed by any formal permit applications. Until those steps occur, the most defensible description is a significant expansion under consideration—one that could change Lincoln’s winter economy, but is still years from a possible opening and may never be built as currently drawn.
location: Loon Mountain Resort, Lincoln, New Hampshire
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Loon Mountain proposes fourth peak in Lincoln, New Hampshire
seoDescription: Loon Mountain has proposed 280 acres of new terrain, four lifts and two lodges near downtown Lincoln, but the project still needs federal and local approval.
